title: Understanding Bag-of-Words
text: Think about how the bag-of-words model works. It counts the frequency of each word in a document. In this case, consider what 'words' might mean for DNA sequences.

title: Identifying the 'Words'
text: In the context of DNA sequences, what could be considered as 'words'? Remember, DNA sequences are made up of codons, which are groups of three letters.

title: Calculating Possible Combinations
text: Each codon is made up of $$3$$ letters, and each letter can be one of $$4$$ types (T, G, C, A). How many different codons can you form?

title: Possible Codons
text: How many different codons can be formed from the $$4$$ DNA bases?

title: Connecting to Bag-of-Words
text: Now that you know the number of possible codons, think about how this relates to the dimensions in a bag-of-words model. Each unique codon represents a dimension.
